vocabulary.definition: A branch of biology dealing with the study of fungi.
A group of artists who sought to restore artistic principles from before Raphael.
The act of producing an offspring of two animals or plants of different breeds.
A complex organism made of an alga and a fungus growing in symbiotic association.
Green with vegetation; lush and covered in plants or grass.
The animals characteristic of a particular region, period, or special environment.
Applying multiple layers of material where underlying layers are completely hidden.

timeline.event: Beatrix Potter is born in London.
Beatrix paints 'Fly agaric', showing her growing sophistication.
Beatrix meets her mentor, Charles McIntosh, for the first time.

artworks.title: Study of a Bat
artworks.description: A precise anatomical drawing showing the wing structure of a nocturnal mammal.

artworks.title: Fly Agaric
artworks.description: A painting of a red-capped toadstool situated among moss and pine needles.

artworks.title: Peter Rabbit
artworks.description: An illustration of a rabbit in a blue jacket eating a radish.

artworks.title: The Tailor of Gloucester
artworks.description: Intricate illustrations featuring mice sewing clothes, known for their period detail.

locations.name: Eastwood
locations.significance: The house in Dunkeld where she met Charles McIntosh.

locations.name: Hill Top Farm
locations.significance: The farm she purchased in the Lake District which inspired many books.

locations.name: Bolton Gardens
locations.significance: Her childhood home in Kensington, London.

locations.name: Perth Museum
locations.significance: The museum where Charles McIntosh's drawings, and later Potter's fungi studies, were kept.

trueFalse.statement: Beatrix Potter was born in Scotland.
trueFalse.correction: She was born in London at 2 Bolton Gardens.

trueFalse.statement: Mycology is the study of mosses and ferns.
trueFalse.correction: Mycology is the study of fungi.

trueFalse.statement: Charles McIntosh was a postman who became an expert naturalist.
trueFalse.correction: He was indeed a rural postman and a respected naturalist.

trueFalse.statement: Potter's parents were very supportive of her scientific ambitions.
trueFalse.correction: Her parents, particularly her mother, discouraged her scientific interests.

quiz.question: Who was the Scottish postman and naturalist who mentored Beatrix Potter?
